title: Festivals Around the World
description: Four recordings about festivals: a radio interview, an announcement, a conversation and a podcast about Tet.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · A radio interview
parts.intro: You will hear Mai interviewing Daniel, who loves visiting festivals.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Welcome to Culture Corner. Today we're talking about festivals, and my guest is Daniel, who has travelled to more than twenty countries to join them.

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: Thanks, Mai. It's a pleasure. Although to be honest, I only count the ones I really enjoyed, so maybe it's closer to eighteen.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Which festival surprised you most?

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: Probably the lantern festival in northern Thailand. I expected a quiet event, but thousands of people were in the fields, and everyone released a paper lantern at the same time. The sky turned orange. I'd never seen anything like it.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Was it difficult to get a place?

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: Very. The tickets sold out in March, and the festival is in November. I was lucky because a friend of mine knew the organiser.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: And what's your advice for people who want to go to a big festival?

script.speaker: Daniel
script.text: Book early, and don't carry too much. Most people bring huge bags, then they spend the whole day worrying about them. A small bag, a bottle of water and a camera are enough.

script.speaker: Mai
script.text: Good advice. Thank you, Daniel.

parts.title: Part 2 · A festival announcement
parts.intro: You will hear an announcement at a food festival.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Good morning, and welcome to the Riverside Food Festival. Before you start tasting, please listen to a few important announcements.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: First, the festival opens at ten o'clock and closes at nine in the evening. Last year it closed at eight, but so many people asked for extra time that we changed it.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Second, the cooking competition was planned for the main stage, but because of the rain forecast, it will take place in the big green tent near the bridge. It begins at two o'clock, not at noon as the programme says.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Third, if you are looking for a quiet place to sit and eat, the library garden is open to everyone. Please remember to take your plates back to the stalls, because we want to keep the river clean.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Finally, children under twelve can join our free pancake workshop at four o'clock. You don't need to book, but there are only twenty places, so please arrive early. Enjoy the festival!

parts.title: Part 3 · Choosing a festival
parts.intro: You will hear two friends, Hannah and Nam, talking about summer plans.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Nam, have you decided which festival to go to this summer? The music one or the colour festival?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Well, I was thinking about the colour festival, because my cousin went last year and said it was fantastic. But then I read that you finish the day covered in powder from head to toe.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: That's the whole point! Everybody throws coloured powder, and it's meant to celebrate the arrival of spring.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: I know, but I'm not sure about my clothes. I'd have to throw away everything I wear.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Not really. You just wear old white clothes. I did it two years ago, and I still use the same shirt for painting.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Hmm. What about the music festival, then? It's cheaper, isn't it?

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: Actually, it isn't. The tickets for the music festival cost eighty pounds, and the colour festival is only fifty. But the music one lasts three days, so you also need a tent.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Right. That's a lot of extra money. And I hate sleeping outside.

script.speaker: Hannah
script.text: So the colour festival sounds better for you. And it's just one day, so you can go home to your own bed.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: You've convinced me. Let's book tonight.

parts.title: Part 4 · A podcast about Tet
parts.intro: You will hear Minh, a student, talking about a holiday in his country.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Hello, everybody, and welcome to our school podcast. This week I'd like to tell you about Tet, the Lunar New Year, which is the most important holiday in my country.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Tet usually falls in January or February, and families start getting ready weeks before. People clean the house, because they believe it sweeps away bad luck from the old year. However, you must not sweep on the first day, or you might sweep away good luck too.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: One of my favourite traditions is making sticky rice cakes. My grandmother starts at six in the evening, and we sit around the pot all night, telling stories. Many of my friends find that boring, but for me it's the best part of the holiday.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: On the first morning, children put on new clothes and visit relatives. The adults give us small red envelopes with money inside. I used to spend it all on sweets, but now I save most of it.

script.speaker: Minh
script.text: Some visitors think Tet is only about food and presents, but it's really about family. Even people who live far away try to come home, and the trains and buses are full for days. If you ever get the chance to celebrate Tet in Vietnam, I'm sure you'll never forget it.
